summary: The People screen can now say what face recognition DOES, and choose what it alerts on. THE GAP: enrolling somebody and switching on a camera produces an alert with a boxed snapshot, an event clip, a notification to every configured destination, and optionally a PTZ recall and a relay — every one of which lands on a DIFFERENT screen. From the People page the feature was indistinguishable from one that does nothing. Three additions. (1) WHAT IT ALERTS ON, per camera: 'Anyone enrolled' (a staff door), 'Only chosen people' (a watchlist, with the names picked inline) or 'Unknown faces' (strangers, a perimeter). All three modes have worked in infra/vision/face.go since face rules shipped and NOTHING in the UI could select between them — stranger detection existed and could not be switched on. The include mode does not save at the moment it is chosen, because the server refuses a watchlist with nobody on it (correctly: it would alert on no one); the row opens the list and commits with the first name ticked, rather than posting something that comes back as an error. (2) LAST SEEN, on each person's card: 'Seen 4 minutes ago on Lobby Entrance', from a new GET /api/faces/sightings that reduces a bounded window of recent face alerts to the latest per person. It reads the alert log rather than keeping a tally — the alert IS the record, and a second counter would be a second thing to keep true. Unrecognized faces are reported separately ('2 unrecognized faces seen recently'), because they belong to nobody and a screen showing only known people would otherwise hide that strangers are being seen. (3) A line saying what a match actually does, shown once a camera is on. WHAT THE BENCH FOUND, both invisible to unit tests: the camera row was a flex ROW holding two blocks, so the camera's on/off switch came to sit ON TOP of the first watchlist checkbox — ticking the first person in a watchlist switched the camera off instead, and the harness only caught it because it asserts document.elementFromPoint before every click; and the base stylesheet's `input, select, textarea { width: 100% }` turned the mode dropdown into a full-width bar that squeezed the camera name to nothing and the checkboxes into large empty boxes.
compatibility: Backward-compatible. ONE NEW ROUTE, GET /api/faces/sightings (admin-only by the same catalog row as the rest of /api/faces; `?scan=` bounds the window, default 500, max 2000). No schema change: it reads existing alert_event rows and needs no index beyond the cam_time/time ones already there. Existing face rules keep working untouched — a rule with no matchMode still means 'known', which is what the parser has always defaulted to. The People page and the rules editor write an explicit minConfidence into every rule they save, which means their value BEATS the server default for any rule they touch. That copy is FACE_MIN_CONFIDENCE in the frontend helpers and it is now 0.4, matching the server floor that a later change in this same batch (mymatasan-face-live-detection) measured and set - the two were briefly out of step, which would have pinned every UI-authored rule to the disproven 0.6 and left that fix reaching nothing anybody had created. A new source-scanning test (TestFaceConfidenceDefaultsAgree in apps/mymatasan) reads both files and fails the build if they drift again. RULES CREATED BEFORE THIS still carry an explicit 0.6 and are left alone rather than rewritten: nothing silently edits a threshold on a running site. Re-saving such a rule - or switching its camera off and on from the People page - picks up 0.4; setting the value by hand in the camera's AI rules editor keeps whatever is chosen. Frontend adds 21 dictionary keys in en/ms/zh/ar, drops one dead key, and the built-in manual gains two sections (#what-happens, #alert-modes) on the People page in all four languages.
